candidate.answerReason: The sum of the squared median lengths is 5/4 times the sum of the squared legs. Thus the hypotenuse squared is (4/5)(25+40)=52.

methods.label: Apply the Pythagorean theorem to the medians
methods.explanation:
Let \(\triangle ABC\) have its right angle at \(C\), with \(AC=u>0\) and \(BC=v>0\). Label the acute vertices so that the median from \(A\) has length \(5\) and the median from \(B\) has length \(\sqrt{40}\).

A median ends at the midpoint of the opposite side. The median from \(A\) therefore forms a right triangle whose legs are \(u\) and \(v/2\). Similarly, the median from \(B\) forms a right triangle whose legs are \(v\) and \(u/2\). The Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
u^2+\frac{v^2}{4}=25,
\qquad
v^2+\frac{u^2}{4}=40.
\]
We need \(u^2+v^2\), rather than either leg separately, so add the equations:
\[
\frac54(u^2+v^2)=25+40=65.
\]
Thus
\[
u^2+v^2=52.
\]
The hypotenuse has square \(52\) and positive length, so it is
\[
\sqrt{52}=2\sqrt{13},
\]
choice D.
methods.levelReason: The median definition produces two right triangles; adding their Pythagorean equations and simplifying a square root completes the solution.

candidate.annotationRationale: The task connects the definition of a median with right-triangle lengths. Midpoints provide the half-leg lengths, and the Pythagorean theorem supplies all three length relations. Adding the equations reveals the needed sum directly, without solving a two-variable system or invoking a general median-length formula.
